333CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  August 24 2020 - 2:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Tomek called the special meeting to order at 2:02 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember McAustin.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Terry T ornek
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Victor Gordo
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Margaret McAustin
  Councilmember Andy Wilson

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Councilmember McAustin spoke on the City's scheduled events
  commemorating the 100th Anniversary of the Women's Right to
  Vote, Women's Equality Day (Wednesday, August 6,2020), the
  cancellation of recent and future events due to the pandemic, and
  the new all virtual social media campaign designed to encourage
  residents to register to vote.

  Mayor Tomek requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory
  of those that have suffered due to death and illness caused by
  COVI D-19 in Pasadena, the nation and around the world.

DISCUSSED SEPARATELY  YEAR 2021 PUBLIC HEALTH DEPARTMENT OPERATING
  BUDGET AND INCREASE THE DEPARTMENTAL PERSONNEL
  ALLOCATION BY 6.0 FULL-TIME EQUIVALENT (FTE) FOR THE
  COVID-19 EPIDEMIOLOGY AND LABORATORY CAPACITY
  (ELC) PROGRAM
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  ( 1) Find that the proposed action is not subject to the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines
  Sections 15060(c)(2), 15060(c)(3), and 15378, as the activity will not
  result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in
  the environment;
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract with Los
  Angeles County to accept and administer federal grant funds on behalf
  of the City of Pasadena to expand epidemiology, surveillance, and
  testing capacity to combat COVID-19;
  (3) Adopt a resolution establishing new classifications and setting
  salary control rates for Public Health Nurse Manager and
  Epidemiologist Analyst; and

Council Minutes  2  08/24/2020
   (4) Amend the Fiscal Year 2021 Public Health Department operating
  budget by recognizing and appropriating $1,966,000 in Los Angeles
  County grant pass-through funding from the Centers for Disease
  Control & Prevention and increase the departmental personnel
  allocation by 6.0 new full-time equivalent (FTE) limited-term grant-
  funded positions. (Resolution No. 9803, Budget Amendment No.
  2021-08)

  Mark Jomsky, City Clerk, read aloud comments from Phyllis Chestang,
  Altadena resident, in support of the staff recommendation. He also
  reported that one letter of correspondence was received from Ms.
  Chestang in support of the staff recommendation.

  Vice Mayor Hampton reiterated his request for infomiation on the City's
  Health Department's plan to inspect the senior care facilities in the City.
  He also spoke on the need for the Health Department to provide grief
  counselors to City residents when in need of mental health support.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Tomek, seconded by
  Councilmember McAustin, to approve the staff recommendation:

  Tomek

OLD BUSINESS  CREATION OF A COMMUNITY POLICE OVERSIGHT
  COMMISSION AND AN INDEPENDENT AUDITOR
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council direct
  the City Attorney to prepare and return with an ordinance amending
  the Pasadena Municipal Code, within 30 days, establishing a
  Community Police Oversight Commission and an Independent
  Auditor function as described in the Background section of the
  agenda report.

Council Minutes  4  08/24/2020
   Councilmember Kennedy, Chair of the Public Safety Committee,
  spoke on the need to provide community oversight to the Pasadena
  Police Department, and spoke in favor of establishing a Community
  Police Oversight Commission (CPOC). Mayor Terry Tomek
  summarized the agenda report, including the modifications related
  to the composition of a proposed CPOC, and the Independent
  Police Auditor (IPA) appointment process; and responded to
  questions.

  Councilmember Madison expressed disappointment on the lack of
  detailed information in the agenda report, including the lack of a
  fiscal impact statement; and spoke on the need for further
  discussion on the details pertaining to the creation of a CPOC and
  IPA. He spoke in favor of the City Council moving forward with
  police oversight with true independence, which he believes is the
  City Council, who are accountable to the voters, and an IPA that
  would report through the City Manager's Office to the City Council
  and the CPOC. He expressed concerns with placing an IPA in the
  City Attorney's Office, which he believes creates a conflict of
  interest and lack of independence, and a constitutional crisis under
  the City's Charter.

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided information on staff's
  communication related to the consultant that provided an analysis
  on police oversight in 2016, and staff's effort to update the City's
  2016 analysis by retrieving information from various City's (listed in
  the analysis); and responded to questions.

  Michele Beal Bagneris, City Attorney/City Prosecutor, provided
  information on the legal requirement for the City Council to take an
  action as a body, and the required information to be included in the
  City's agenda reports; and responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor Hampton expressed concerns with the release of the
  video and information related to the Pasadena Police Officer
  Involved Shooting (01S) of Anthony McClain without the knowledge
  of the City Council. He spoke in opposition to community members
  being cited and pulled over for missing license plates. He asked
  staff for detailed information regarding the OIS, including why
  officers chased Mr. McClain, why the officer did not engage his
  body-worn camera, details of the shooting, public endangerment
  issues committed by the officer, questions regarding the
  investigation where the officer's body worn camera was turned off,
  and why the officer has not been fired for acting out of policy.

  Councilmember Gordo expressed concerns as to why his request
  of a thorough analysis of true independent accountability that is
  separate from the City Manager's Office was not provided by staff.
  He stated that anytime the City Council is asked to delegate any
  authority, the community and the City Council has the right to see

Council Minutes  5  08/24/2020
   such an analysis in writing. He reiterated his request for information
  on a model CPOC and IPA that does not require Charter reform
  with an IPA placed in the City Attorney's Office, by contracting an
  IPA that will report directly to the City Council.

  Javan Rad, Chief Assistant City Attorney, provided information on
  the definition of a "compelled statement," and responded to
  questions.

  Councilmember Masuda restated his position that the highest form
  of police oversight is the Public Safety Committee and the City
  Council. He expressed concerns with an IPA placed in the City
  Attorney's Office; and stated his preference that members of a
  CPOC be nominated by the City Council in order to ensure there is
  balance in the Commission's membership.

  Vice Mayor Hampton stated his preference that the IPA position be
  hired as an independent contractor, with a contractual agreement
  to report directly to the City Council; and expressed concerns as to
  why such an option was not presented to the PSC as additional
  options for civilian police oversight.

  Councilmember Gordo stated for the record, "That is exactly the
  model that I asked be analyzed ... exactly that model."

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke in favor of the recommendation to
  direct staff to prepare an ordinance amending the Pasadena
  Municipal Code (PMC) to establish a Community Police Oversight
  Commission (CPOC) and an Independent Police Auditor (IPA).

  Councilmember McAustin spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation as a starting point for the implementation of a
  CPOC and IPA. She stated her preference that an IPA report
  directly to the City Council and CPOC, and that the IPA be a
  contractor and not a direct employee. She also expressed a strong
  desire to include a prequalification process to be implemented for
  individuals that would like to apply to become a member of the
  CPOC. The prequalification includes all applicants be required to
  complete training and participate on a ride-along with a Pasadena
  Police Officer; and recommended that the City provide child care
  assistance to provide support during training and/or ride-alongs.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with the
  recommendation and stated his preference that a recommendation
  on police oversight should come from the City Council with
  additional current information on best practices. He spoke in favor
  of separating the City Attorney and City Prosecutor Offices. In
  addition, the creation of a CPOC utilizing the City's regular
  commission models with training to be completed in advance. He
  would also like the training to include the Citizens Police Academy.
  He expressed concerns with the proposed 13 members to make up
  a CPOC, and recommended 9 members with each councilmember,
  the Mayor and the City Manager to provide an appointee. He stated
  preference that all CPOC members live in the City and that each
  Councilmember appoint a member that resides in their respective
  districts. He also spoke in favor of an IPA that reports directly to the
  City Council, with the position to be established outside the City
  Attorney's Office. He defines reporting as; the IPA will create

Council Minutes  15  08/24/2020
   reports related to the City's public safety policies, practices,
  procedures, individual cases, and elevating the City's best
  practices. Such reports should go to the City Council, City Manager,
  Chief of Police, and the CPOC. However, related to whomever
  gives direction to the IPA, should be directly to and from the City
  Council not the CPOC. In addition, he stated his preference that the
  CPOC and IPA should make presentations and reports at the Public
  Safety Committee (PSC). Councilmember Madison expressed
  concerns with the subpoena power issue, which he believes is a
  "red-herring." The City Council has the authority to issue
  subpoenas, however, he is not sure the City Council is able to
  delegate such authority. He stated that the City Council must be
  clear that the IPA is reporting and taking direction from the City
  Council, and that it would be appropriate to delegate subpoena
  power to the extent that it is legal to do so in the City Charter. He
  also suggested that the City consider using the County of Los
  Angeles' Inspector General (costs are associated for such use),
  which is a sensible independent auditor option with expertise.

  The Mayor expressed concerns with including the issue of
  separating the City Attorney and City Prosecutor in the motion
  without information or discussion on the merits of separating the
  two positions.

  Councilmember Gordo spoke in favor of separating the functions of
  the City Attorney and City Prosecutor as an additional form of
  transparency; and expressed concerns with the lack of analysis and
  information from staff on an Inspector General, CPOC, and IPA. He
  also expressed concerns with the process of the current model that
  excluded input from Councilmember Madison, Vice Mayor
  Hampton, other members of the City Council, and the community to
  provide input on the CPOC and IPA. He also spoke in favor of the
  City Council utilizing the County of Los Angeles' Inspector General
  as an opportunity to review Police Officer involved use of force
  incidents. Councilmember Gordo spoke in support of
  Councilmember Madison's substitute motion and requested that the
  substitute motion be amended to ensure that an Independent
  Inspector General can commence working immediately on the 01S
  of Anthony McClain.

  In response to Councilmember McAustin' s inquiry to summarize
  his substitute motion, Councilmember Madison responded that his
  amendment to the motion includes: the use of County of Los
  Angeles' Inspector General, a CPOC made up of 9 nominated
  members approved by the City Council (one nomination per City
  Council district and the City Manager), members of CPOC would
  live within the districts they are nominated from, members of the
  CPOC receive 30 hours of training (preferably in advance) and have
  graduated or enrolled in the City's Community Police Academy
  (when feasible), and an IPA that would prepare reports for the City

Council Minutes  16  08/24/2020
   Council, CPOC, City Manager, Police Chief and community, but
  would take direction from the City Council and through the Public
  Safety Community, and the IPA would have subpoena power to the
  extent such is legally delegated by the City Council.

  Councilmember Masuda spoke in favor of the Tomek/Kennedy
  model of a creation of CPOC and IPA; and in favor of each
  Councilmember nominating a CPOC member for City Council
  approval.

  Councilmember Wilson stated that the proposal to split the City
  Attorney and City Prosecutor may be a valid move, but he is not
  prepared to take a position on that issue at this time without
  sufficient data and further opportunity for deliberation. He stated he
  does not believe the Tomek/Kennedy proposal was formulated
  behind the scenes and spoke on the need to find a path forward to
  be responsive to the community. He spoke in favor of the
  KennedyIT ornek recommendation.

  Vice Mayor Hampton stated that he does not believe CPOC
  members should be mandated to take the 30 hours of training prior
  to being selected. He suggested to provide an appropriate time
  frame to allow the members to complete the mandatory training. He
  expressed concerns with the Independent Review process, which
  he believes it is an "after the fact investigation", and would prefer a
  "real time" review of the Pasadena Police Department. He asked
  the City Manager to conduct a totally independent investigation of
  the OIS of Anthony McClain. He also requested that the IPA
  workload include such reviews of PPD in real time. He spoke in
  favor of the amended motion, specifically that the IPA is
  independent of the City Manager.

  City Manager Mermell provided information on his plans to solicit
  proposals from consultants to conduct an independent review of the
  OIS of Anthony McClain; and responded to questions. Javan Rad,
  Chief Assistant City Attorney, provided general information on the
  City's actions related to Independent Reviews of officer involved
  shootings; and responded to questions.

  Councilmember McAustin spoke on the need to be transparent
  when Councilmembers nominate and the City Council appoints
  members to the CPOC, and advocated for a public process which
  includes an application, attending a City Council meeting, public
  review of individual resumes, and providing an opportunity for
  applicants to express their interests in becoming CPOC members.
  She does not agree that members should be appointed by district,
  and advocated for two or three members to be chosen from
  community organizations (i.e. ACLU, non-profit organization). She
  shared information from her constituents related to CPOC, including
  the need for diversity in memberships, overlapping terms to ensure

Council Minutes  17  08/24/2020
   consistency in membership, and representation by community
  groups most impacted by policing issues. She also suggested
  providing stipends or allowances for child care or other expenses
  that may be incurred when attending CPOC meetings. She stated
  that she is unable to support the substitute motion, as she prefers
  a more responsive process to the community for transparency.

  Councilmember Kennedy stated that he is not supportive of the
  substitute motion as there has not been adequate discussion
  centered on the bifurcation of the City Attorney/City Prosecutor
  Office. He noted, however, that is agreeable to incorporating
  elements of the substitute motion to the proposed recommended
  creation of a CPOC and IPA. He spoke in favor of the CPOC
  members be made up 50% women.

  Mayor Tomek spoke in favor of representation from each of the City
  Council and Mayor, and citywide representation from non-profit
  organizations (on a rotating basis) for a total of 11 members. He
  spoke in favor of vetting CPOC members by inviting applicant's to
  complete applications and conduct interviews in the public view. He
  stated that he believes it is impractical to request applicants to
  complete training as a prerequisite to serving on the CPOC, as he
  would like to move forward with implementing CPOC as quickly as
  possible.

  Councilmember Madison spoke on the need for the City Council to
  come to an agreement and move forward; and stated that he is
  prepared to withdraw the first part portion of his motion (the
  bifurcation of the City Prosecutor and City Attorney), however he
  would like to agendize at a future City Council meeting a discussion
  to consider the bifurcation of City Prosecutor and City Attorney
  positions. He reiterated his request that advanced training is
  attainable and desirable; and he is acceptable to 11 members of a
  CPOC made up of the Mayor, City Councilmembers appointees and
  3 community members.

  Councilmember McAustin stated that training for CPOC members
  should be independent training not from the Pasadena Police
  Department; and asked staff to provide information including
  expenditure and time frame for such training. She also spoke in
  favor of creating a "wait list" or "qualified list of candidates" in the
  event a sitting CPOC member needs to step down, to avoid lengthy
  vacancies and delays in appointing replacements.

  Councilmember Gordo expressed concerns with the proposed 30
  hours of training for CPOC members as insufficient to understand
  the complexity of policing issues; and requested that the members
  receive additional hours and on-going training. He spoke on the
  importance of the City Council retaining "direct report" authority of
  the IPNlnspector General, as well as the ability to make

Council Minutes  18  08/24/2020
   recommendations to the CPOC to review in advance the Pasadena
  Police Department's policies, such as Use of Force, Traffic Stops,
  and other community policing policies, to ensure the City is
  employing best practices, procedures, and policies. The
  IPA/Inspector General should have authority to give the City
  Council and CPOC recommendations on practices that keeps the
  public safe and ensures the Police Department is operating and
  training at its best.

  Councilmember Wilson spoke on the need to track the progress of
  the Pasadena Police Department, the CPOC, and the IPA, as well
  as the need to develop performance metrics to monitor progress,
  and determine if Charter reform should be considered; with staff to
  recommend and the City Council to establish a feedback and
  benchmark system.

  Following discussion, the Mayor summarized the original motion to
  include the following:

  •  The City Council will direct staff to return to the City Council
  with language on the creation a Community Police Oversight
  Commission (CPOC) and an Independent Police Auditor
  (IPA);
  •  The CPOC will consist of 11 members (a combination of one
  nominee by each Councilmember and the Mayor, and 3 at
  large community based organizations, to be approved by the
  City Council);
  •  Staff will provide suggestions regarding a public process for
  the appointment of members to the CPOC, with the idea of
  having a method for public vetting of the applicants;
  •  Staff to provide a mechanism for the selection of the 3
  community organizations appointees to CPOC;
  •  Approving the general purpose and required training of
  CPOC members, as described in the agenda report;
  •  Clarification with regards to the role of the Public Safety
  Committee(PSC) with the intent that the PSC will continue to
  maintain its general responsibilities, CPOC to strive to avoid
  duplication of work, effort, repetitive reporting, and not to pre-
  empt the role of PSC;
  •  The IPA will be hired through the City Attorney's Office as a
  financial intermediary;
  •  The IPA is anticipated to be a firm rather than an individual,
  and will report to the City Council and CPOC;
  •  The IPA will have subpoena powers (independent of the City
  Council and CPOC);
  •  With regards to the investigatory role, there will be
  exploration and exposition on how the IPA may observe the
  investigation in "real time" as apposed to conclusions
  reached at the end;

Council Minutes  19  08/24/2020
   •  It is understood that consideration of the bifurcation of the
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor functions will be agendized at
  a future City Council meeting no later than October 2020;
  •  Direct staff to provide recommendations on potential
  stipends (i.e. for childcare) for CPOC members; and
  •  Direct staff to provide a concept on reporting and developing
  performance metrics to track CPOC's progress.

  Councilmembers McAustin, Wilson and Gordo thanked and
  acknowledged _Councilmember Kennedy, Mayor Tomek, and Vice
  Mayor Hampton, for all their hard work on police oversight.
